text_transform: scripts.utils.transliteration.normalize_iso (via convert_text(text, 'iso', 'iso')): NFC + diphthong-accent shift + precomposed-vocalic-r rewrite — the transform experiment_accent_ratio.evaluate_on_dataset applied before writing the committed accent counts
alt_text_transform: scripts.evaluation.prediction_metrics.DEFAULT_NORMALIZATION (NFC + strip, no diphthong shift) — the study evaluator's convention; reported per view as alt_normalization, not used for the decomposition
misplacement_window_zero_note: Window 0 is a degenerate control, not a smaller version of the others: a hypothesis mark in the SAME slot as an unmatched reference mark would have been scored a match, so same-slot pairs are structurally almost impossible in the observed data while the rotated null is free to produce them. Its excess is therefore large and negative by construction and carries no information; the informative windows are 1 and above.

class_definitions.matched_same_kind: The aligned hypothesis syllable carries a mark of the same kind. The only non-error class; equals the committed accent_tp_labeled.
class_definitions.matched_other_kind: The aligned hypothesis syllable carries a mark of the OTHER kind (acute where grave belongs, or the reverse). Counted as a true positive by the unlabelled accent F1 and as both a false negative and a false positive by the labelled one — which is the entire difference between accent_f1 and accent_f1_labeled, lifted out here rather than recomputed.
class_definitions.no_mark_at_read_syllable: The aligned hypothesis position is the SAME base code point and carries no mark: the syllable was read, the mark was not written. Named for what is observed at the position and deliberately NOT called 'omitted': whether the mark is missing from the output or present elsewhere in it is not decidable from one position — read hyp_marks_per_ref_accent and the misplacement refinement for that.
class_definitions.ref_syllable_misread: The aligned hypothesis position is a different code point, or the reference character has no counterpart at all (a deletion). The letter itself is wrong, so no accent judgement about that syllable is meaningful — reported, never credited.
class_definitions.extra_at_read_syllable: A hypothesis mark on a syllable whose base code point matches the reference's and which the reference leaves unaccented: a mark invented on a correctly read letter.
class_definitions.extra_at_misread_syllable: A hypothesis mark on a syllable whose base code point differs from the reference's, or which the hypothesis inserted outright.

diagnostic_counts.hyp_marks_per_ref_accent: n_hyp_accent_vowels / n_ref_accent_vowels: how many marks the model wrote per mark the reference has. Not a class — the number that decides whether a channel with a low F1 is writing FEWER marks (a channel that went quiet) or about as many in the wrong places (a channel that went random). Reading a low accent F1 as omission without it is an inference the data need not support.
diagnostic_counts.matched_on_substituted_base: Subset of matched_same_kind + matched_other_kind: the mark matched although the base letter did not, so the accent channel is credited for a syllable the base channel got wrong.
diagnostic_counts.n_ref_accent_marks_nfd: Every U+0301 / U+0300 in the NFD reference, whether or not it sits on a vowel. NOT the decomposition's denominator — see letter_s_acute_note.
diagnostic_counts.n_ref_accent_marks_on_letter_s: Subset of n_ref_accent_marks_nfd: U+0301 marks that are the second half of the ISO letter ś (s + U+0301), i.e. consonants, not accents.
diagnostic_counts.n_ref_accent_marks_unanchored_other: n_ref_accent_marks_nfd minus n_ref_accent_vowels minus n_ref_accent_marks_on_letter_s: NFD accent code points that are neither vowel-anchored nor part of an ś. Expected 0; reported so it cannot be zero by assumption.

letter_s_acute_note: U+0301 is both the high-accent mark and the second half of the ISO letter ś (NFC U+015B decomposes to s + U+0301). A count of 'accent marks' taken over the NFD reference therefore includes every ś in the corpus, and an accent-vs-base split that tests membership of the edited code point in an accent set charges ś edits to the accent channel. The accent channel used here is anchored on vowel bases (accent_metrics._vowel_positions), so ś is structurally excluded — which is also why the reference denominator (n_ref_accent_vowels) is smaller than the NFD accent-mark count. Both are reported per view, with the ś share measured, so the gap is evidence rather than a claim.

reference_set_identity.note: One hash across every (cell, view) is the parallel-by-text property: the notation contrast is image-only. This hash CANNOT attest the corpus — v2 re-renders the same ISO text as v1, so it is identical across corpora by construction. Corpus identity is the Slurm-header attestation.

alignment_self_check.why: scripts/evaluation/accent_metrics.py is inside the shared metric implementation's source lock, so the event-emitting hook this analysis wants cannot be added there. The alignment walk is restated in this module and its charging rule imported unchanged; this per-view equality against compute_accent_metrics is the guard that replaces the shared code path.

subset_consistency.held_fixed_scope: grid-wide across every present cell; key_list_sha256 is excluded on purpose and checked per seed instead (key_list_sha256_scope)
subset_consistency.key_list_sha256_scope: constant WITHIN each seed across the five ratios; expected to DIFFER across seeds (3 distinct values for a healthy grid)
subset_consistency.key_list_sha256_note: key_list_sha256 hashes the ordered shared-parallel ISO *text* keys. The v2 corpus re-renders the SAME text, so this hash is identical between v1 and v2 by construction and CANNOT attest which image corpus a cell consumed. Use corpus_attestation (Slurm .out header) for that.
subset_consistency.key_list_sha256_seed_note: key_list_sha256 hashes the ORDERED selected key list, and the selection is seeded: scripts/training/trocr/dataset.py sorts the shared keys and then applies a seeded shuffle (the launcher leaves parallel_subset_seed=null, so it follows `seed`). At full N the selected key SET is identical across seeds while its ORDER — hence the hash — is not. The hash is therefore a WITHIN-SEED invariant, constant across the five ratios of one seed and EXPECTED to differ across seeds: a healthy 15-cell grid has exactly 3 distinct values, one per seed. It is checked that way (key_list_sha256_per_seed) and is NOT a grid-wide held-fixed field; a cross-seed recipe split is still caught by the grid-wide fields, which include model_base and total_train_samples_requested.

corpus_attestation.source: immutable Slurm .out header echoed by the launcher

corpus_attestation.note: Absence of a log means UNATTESTED, not v1. results.json records no corpus path, so an unattested cell's corpus is established only from its W&B config / Hydra snapshot. Attestation matches a log to a cell by run name, which the _smoke study root reuses verbatim — study_root_mismatches lists any matched log whose own output_dir echo belongs to a different study root. The corpus= token is a LABEL, not evidence (RV_DATA_DIR/MS_DATA_DIR are launcher overrides): corpus_mismatches lists every attested cell whose echoed data dirs or data_source do not establish the expected v2 corpus, which is what single_corpus cannot catch — it sees mixtures, not a uniformly wrong corpus.

grid_integrity.note: read_cell_dir takes a cell's seed from its results.json while the run dir name encodes the requested seed, so these are two independent records of the same fact and must agree. A ratio whose present cells do not carry distinct seeds is not an n-seed result no matter what n the table prints.
